name: Gangaramaya Temple
description: A working Colombo temple that doubles as a museum of donated curiosities — vintage cars, carved ivory and crowded relic cabinets sit alongside the shrine hall. The sheer density of objects makes it unlike any other temple interior in the city.
directions: On Sri Jinaratana Road beside Beira Lake, a short walk from Seema Malaka. The lane entrance is narrow and easy to miss coming from Hunupitiya Road.
tips: Interiors are cluttered and dim — a fast lens beats a flash you are not permitted to use.
Shoulders and knees covered, shoes off at the shrine entrance.
The Navam Perahera in February fills the whole precinct with elephants and dancers.
entryFee: Nominal donation requested at the museum section.
droneNotes: Dense urban airspace beside an active religious site; do not fly here.
shootingNotes: Cramped interiors mixing tungsten and daylight — expect heavy white-balance correction.

name: Wellawatte Beach
description: A working city beach rather than a resort one — fishing boats hauled up on the sand, cricket games, and a steady flow of residents walking after work. The coastal railway runs directly behind it.
directions: Reached by level crossings off Galle Road in Wellawatte (Colombo 06). Wellawatte station sits on the beach side of the line.
tips: Trains passing between the sand and the road make a strong foreground element.
Evening is when the beach fills with locals — better for candid work than empty sand.
Litter varies day to day; scout the frame before committing to a wide shot.
droneNotes: Inside Colombo's controlled airspace — CAASL registration and TRCSL clearance required.

name: Viharamahadevi Park
description: The city's oldest and largest park, laid out under British rule as Victoria Park and later renamed for the mother of King Dutugemunu. Mature rain trees, a golden Buddha statue, and the Town Hall dome rising behind the lawns.
directions: Opposite Colombo Town Hall, bounded by Ananda Coomaraswamy Mawatha in Colombo 07. Gates on several sides; the Town Hall side is the usual approach.
tips: Rain-tree canopies hold usable open shade right through the middle of the day.
The Town Hall dome lines up cleanly as a background from the northern lawns.
A nominal admission applies at the gate — carry small change in rupees.
entryFee: Nominal gate fee, around LKR 20 for adults.
droneNotes: Adjacent to government buildings in central Colombo; flying is not permitted.

name: Port City Colombo
description: Reclaimed land north of Galle Face being built out as a new financial district. Wide empty boulevards and a hard geometric seafront give it a character entirely unlike the rest of Colombo.
directions: North of Galle Face Green, entered from the Marine Drive side. Open areas and access points shift as construction phases complete.
tips: Empty new infrastructure suits clean minimal composition and longer lenses.
Security patrols the active zones — ask before setting up near construction.
Almost no shade anywhere; treat it as an early-morning or late-afternoon location.
openingHours: Public promenade areas generally open during daylight.
droneNotes: Port-adjacent restricted airspace with an active security presence.

name: Bentota Beach
description: A broad stretch of sand on the spit where the Bentota river meets the sea, so open surf on one side and still lagoon water on the other sit within a few minutes' walk of each other.
directions: About 65 km south of Colombo on the Galle road, and a stop on the coastal railway. The river mouth is at the northern end of the beach.
tips: The sandbar at the river mouth is the distinctive frame here, not the open beach.
The lagoon side stays glassy at dawn while the sea side is already breaking.
West-facing, so sunset works directly off the sand.
droneNotes: Open coastline clear of controlled airspace; CAASL registration still applies.

name: Weligama Bay
description: A wide shallow bay with a forgiving beach break, which is why most of the south coast's surf schools cluster here. Outrigger fishing boats line the eastern end and a small island sits just offshore.
directions: On the main coast road between Galle and Matara. The bay is visible from the road along its full length, with access points throughout.
tips: Beginner surf means plenty of usable action without needing a long lens.
The fishing fleet at the eastern end is the quieter photographic end of the bay.
Shallow water a long way out suits low-angle reflective work at dawn.

name: Tangalle Beach
description: A long run of far-south coastline broken into separate coves by rocky headlands. Noticeably emptier than the Galle-side beaches, with stronger surf and more open horizon.
directions: About 195 km from Colombo via the southern expressway to Matara, then the coast road. Goyambokka and Medaketiya are the main access coves.
tips: Headlands let you shoot down into a cove rather than along flat sand.
Currents here are genuinely strong — be careful positioning anyone in the water.
Few facilities between coves, so carry everything you need.

name: Dondra Head Lighthouse
description: The southernmost point of the island, marked by a 49 m colonial lighthouse in banded stone. There is nothing but open ocean south of here until Antarctica.
directions: At Devinuwara, roughly 6 km east of Matara. A side road off the coast road runs out to the headland and the lighthouse compound.
tips: The tower reads best against open sky from the rocks below rather than head-on.
Interior access is restricted — plan on exterior frames only.
Exposed headland with constant wind and salt spray; shield your gear.
openingHours: Grounds accessible during daylight; tower interior generally closed.
droneNotes: Active navigational aid — check locally before flying.

name: Ambalangoda Beach
description: A quiet working beach in a town better known for mask carving and devil-dance traditions. Fishing boats and a rocky natural pool at one end give it more structure than a plain sand strip.
directions: About 85 km south of Colombo on the coast road, between Kosgoda and Hikkaduwa. Ambalangoda railway station is close to the sand.
tips: The natural rock pool holds still water for reflections when the sea is rough.
Mask workshops in town are a strong companion subject to the beach itself.
Sunset is unobstructed along the whole west-facing stretch.

name: Hummanaya Blow Hole
description: A sea cave that forces swell up through a vertical rock shaft, throwing spray well above the cliff line. Reckoned to be the second-largest blowhole in the world and at its most dramatic in rough weather.
directions: At Kudawella, off the coast road between Dickwella and Tangalle. A short walk from the parking area leads to the viewing platform.
tips: Rough seas produce the biggest spouts — calm days can be a non-event.
Spray reaches the platform, so a rain cover is not optional here.
Time your bursts with the swell rather than shooting continuously.
entryFee: Small local entrance charge at the viewing area.

name: Ella Rock
description: The larger of Ella's two summits, reached by a route that follows the railway line before climbing through tea and eucalyptus. The top opens onto Ella Gap with the plains far below.
directions: Walk south from Ella station along the track, then take the marked path uphill. Allow around two hours each way; the junctions are poorly signed.
tips: Go at sunrise — the gap fills with cloud later in the morning.
The track section is live railway; stay alert and step well clear of trains.
Route-finding is genuinely confusing, so download an offline map first.
shootingNotes: A long approach on foot — carry only what you can walk two hours with.

name: Diyaluma Falls
description: At 220 m the second-highest waterfall in the country — a single long drop visible straight from the road, with a chain of natural pools on the plateau above it.
directions: On the Koslanda–Wellawaya road. The base view is roadside; the upper pools need a steep 45-minute climb from a signed trailhead nearby.
tips: Roadside gives you the full drop; the upper pools give the infinity-edge frames.
The climb to the top is steep and slippery — not a route for heavy kit.
Flow drops noticeably in the dry season; after rain is far more impressive.

name: Dunhinda Falls
description: A 64 m fall named for the smoky spray it throws off, reached by a rough path through forest. The viewing platform faces it straight on across the gorge.
directions: About 5 km north of Badulla. A rocky 1 km footpath leads from the parking area to the viewpoint, with stalls along the way.
tips: Constant mist on the platform — keep a cloth on the front element.
The path is uneven rock, so a monopod travels better than a tripod here.
Morning light reaches into the gorge before the sun drops behind the ridge.
entryFee: Small entrance charge at the trailhead.

name: Demodara Railway Loop
description: An engineering answer to a steep gradient: the line spirals under itself and passes through a tunnel directly beneath the station platform, so trains emerge a level below where they entered.
directions: Demodara station, a few kilometres from Ella on the Badulla line. The loop and tunnel mouth are a short walk from the platform.
tips: Check the timetable — the loop only makes sense photographically with a train on it.
The tunnel mouth below the platform is the frame that explains the design.
Station staff are used to photographers, but ask before crossing any track.
openingHours: Station hours; tracks are live at all times.
droneNotes: Railway property — permission from Sri Lanka Railways needed for drone work.

name: Nanu Oya Railway Station
description: The hill-country station serving Nuwara Eliya, and the usual boarding point for the tea-estate rail run towards Ella. Colonial-era platform buildings sit among pines and frequent mist.
directions: About 8 km west of Nuwara Eliya town, connected by frequent tuk-tuks and buses.
tips: Platform mist in the early morning is the signature look here.
Arriving trains fill the platform fast — pre-compose before they pull in.
Cold and damp at this altitude; lens condensation is a real problem.
droneNotes: Railway property; clearance required from Sri Lanka Railways.

name: Victoria Park
description: A formal park in the middle of Nuwara Eliya, planted with temperate flowers that will not grow elsewhere in the country. Also a noted spot for migrant hill-country birds.
directions: Central Nuwara Eliya, beside the main road opposite the post office.
tips: Flower beds peak around March to May after the cool season.
Early morning brings the birdlife and the low mist together.
A modest gate fee applies and the park closes before dark.

name: Gregory Lake
description: A reservoir created under British administration, now the centre of Nuwara Eliya's recreation — a walking promenade, hills reflected in still water, and low cloud most mornings.
directions: On the southern edge of Nuwara Eliya town, with a walkway running along the northern shore.
tips: Still mornings give clean hill reflections before the wind picks up.
Mist rolling across the water is common and worth waiting for.
The promenade is paved and level — the easiest hill-country location for heavy kit.
entryFee: Small charge for the lakeside park area.
